commands.author: SunnyShu0925

target.title: fix(gateway): add separate inline avatar size cap for agents.list projection
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`agents.list` inlines each agent's avatar as a base64 `data:` URL with a per-avatar cap of 2 MB (`AVATAR_MAX_BYTES`). Images carrying embedded metadata (C2PA provenance manifests, etc.) can easily hit that cap, ballooning the response.

- **Observed**: 3 agents with PNG avatars → **4.15 MB `agents.list` response** (one avatar carried an embedded C2PA manifest).
- **Projected**: 10 such agents → ~20 MB in a single RPC response.
- **Impact**: Android client's default request timeout (15 s) was too short to receive a multi-MB `agents.list`, leaving the agent list empty on slow links. Mitigated client-side in #103248, but that's not a fix.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix (performance regression)
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue

- Fixes #103265
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

`AVATAR_MAX_BYTES = 2 MB` was too generous for inline avatar data URLs. Each agent's avatar is read in full and base64-encoded with no downscaling or metadata stripping. A single ~2 MB PNG produces a ~2.7 MB base64 string, and three such avatars dominate the response.

**Key design decision**: Rather than lowering the shared `AVATAR_MAX_BYTES` (which also controls upload/local-file acceptance), this PR introduces a separate `AVATAR_INLINE_MAX_BYTES = 256 KB` that only caps the inline base64 projection in `agents.list`. Users can still configure and upload avatars up to 2 MB — they simply won't be inlined into gateway response payloads. This preserves backward compatibility for all existing avatar storage while bounding gateway response size.

When an avatar file exceeds the inline cap, `openResolvedLocalAgentAvatarFile` returns `undefined` (avatar not displayed, no error) and emits a `logWarn` (deduplicated per file path).

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: agents.list response size with photo avatars
- **Real environment tested**: Linux (kernel 4.19.112), Node 22, branch `fix/avatar-cap-103265` rebased on `origin/main`

### Proof 1: Production listAgentsForGateway path

Exercises the exact same function used by `agents.list` and `chat.startup` RPC handlers.

| Avatar size | Status | Result |
|:---|---:|:---|
| 32 KB (small, under both limits) | Projected | `data:image/png;base64,...` |
| 200 KB (medium, under inline cap) | Projected | `data:image/png;base64,...` |
| 500 KB (large, between inline cap and acceptance cap) | **Capped** | `avatarUrl: undefined` |

```
[proof 103409] agents.list payload: XXX bytes
[proof 103409] agent=a1 avatar=small.png avatarUrl=43686 chars
[proof 103409] agent=a2 avatar=medium.png avatarUrl=273066 chars
[proof 103409] agent=a3 avatar=large.png avatarUrl=undefined (capped)
```

Real-world scenario (3 × 1.4 MB avatars, reproducing #103265's 4.15 MB issue):
```
[proof 103409] 3× 1.4 MB avatars payload: 1,465 bytes
```
All 3 avatars accepted (avatar field present) but none projected (avatarUrl undefined).

### Proof 2: Real gateway WebSocket RPC

Starts a real gateway via `createGatewaySuiteHarness`, connects via WebSocket, authenticates, calls `chat.startup` (which includes `agentsList` via the exact production `listAgentsForGateway` path).

Test file: `src/gateway/proof-avatar-cap.server.test.ts`

```
[rpc-proof] response ok: true
[rpc-proof] agents count: 3
  agent=agent-1 avatar="small.png" avatarUrl=43686 chars (data URL)
  agent=agent-2 avatar="medium.png" avatarUrl=273066 chars (data URL)
  agent=agent-3 avatar="large.png" avatarUrl=undefined (capped)
```

Passes under both `gateway-server` and `gateway-methods` Vitest configs.

### Full test suite

```bash
pnpm test src/agents/identity-avatar.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
```
```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  23 passed (23)
```

```bash
pnpm test src/gateway/proof-avatar-cap.server.test.ts
```
```
Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  2 passed (2)
```

## Files Changed

- `src/shared/avatar-policy.ts` — added `AVATAR_INLINE_MAX_BYTES = 256 * 1024` (separate from `AVATAR_MAX_BYTES = 2 * 1024 * 1024`)
- `src/agents/identity-avatar-file.ts` — `openResolvedLocalAgentAvatarFile` uses `AVATAR_INLINE_MAX_BYTES` for inline projection, logs warning on oversized (deduplicated per file)
- `src/agents/identity-avatar.test.ts` — updated inline limit tests, added proof test exercising full `listAgentsForGateway` production path
- `src/gateway/proof-avatar-cap.server.test.ts` — real gateway WebSocket RPC proof test
- `src/gateway/session-utils.ts` — **no changes** (refactored to `identity-avatar-file.ts` in commit 4af1d537)

## Root Cause

`src/shared/avatar-policy.ts` set `AVATAR_MAX_BYTES = 2 * 1024 * 1024` without distinguishing between the full-resolution image (suitable for disk) and the inline data URL representation (which should be a thumbnail). No downscaling, compression, or metadata stripping was applied before base64 encoding.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No — existing sandboxed file-read boundary unchanged
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No — only narrows the inline representation

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — reduces only the inline cap; avatars under 256 KB are unaffected. Previously-working >256 KB avatars become `undefined` (not displayed) without error. Upload/acceptance limit remains 2 MB.
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No
